key_insight: CardioMeta uses a calibrated multi-task model to predict diabetes, hypertension, and cardiovascular disease together while reducing label leakage and emphasizing reliable probabilities over raw accuracy.
clinical_relevance: The approach may support more dependable risk stratification across population surveys and EHRs, especially when clinicians need calibrated estimates that hold up better under shifting data conditions.
method: Shared cardiometabolic encoder with disease-specific gated prediction heads
Primary analysis excludes disease-defining variables to reduce circular prediction
Post-hoc probability calibration plus temporal and external validation across NHANES and MIMIC-IV
evidence_signal: In leakage-reduced temporal validation, the model reached macro-AUROC 0.839, macro-AUPRC 0.536, macro-F1 0.614, and ECE 0.024, but performance dropped under external domain shift on MIMIC-IV.
watch_item: External transportability remains limited, so deployment would require local recalibration and careful subgroup, temporal, and domain-specific validation.
paper_title: CardioMeta: Calibrated Multi-Task Prediction of Diabetes, Hypertension, and Cardiovascular Disease Across Population and EHR Data
